key_insight: Autonomous deep-research AI agents can systematically discover and evaluate drug assets disclosed outside U.S./English channels by combining multilingual retrieval, automated evidence synthesis, and domain-aware scoring—uncovering opportunities missed by traditional workflows.
problem_solved: Overcomes U.S.-centric, English-only scouting gaps by enabling scalable, cross-lingual search and evaluation of global drug discovery sources for investing and business development.
method: Multilingual data ingestion and normalization from patents, regional databases, local journals, company press releases, and gray literature.
Agent pipeline that autonomously retrieves, translates, extracts entities/claims, synthesizes supporting evidence, and computes domain-aware relevance and risk scores.
Evaluation and ranking loop with domain heuristics and human-in-the-loop validation to produce investor/BD-ready candidate dossiers.
impact: Provides a practical blueprint for building production AI/ML pipelines that expand scientific coverage, speed up due diligence, and improve decision quality in pharma scouting and BD. Useful pattern for agents tackling cross-lingual, domain-heavy search and evaluation tasks.
visual_elements: World map heatmap showing concentration of non-U.S. disclosures (patents, papers) with example country callouts
Pipeline flowchart: sources → multilingual retrieval → translation & extraction → evidence synthesis → scoring & human review
Example asset card mockup showing key metadata, confidence score, top evidence snippets, and suggested next actions
Bar/stacked chart comparing language/source coverage and candidate discovery yield vs. baseline (English-only)
paper_title: Hunt Globally: Deep Research AI Agents for Drug Asset Scouting in Investing, Business Development, and Search & Evaluation
paper_authors: Alisa Vinogradova, Vlad Vinogradov, Luba Greenwood, Ilya Yasny, Dmitry Kobyzev
